gaps.term: Bound on T_A(n) from the cited paper
gaps.quote: The paper proves (cited), so $\lg n$ is replaced by $(\lg n)^{1-\kappa}$, a smaller power of the logarithm.
gaps.note: The page never states the bound the paper proves on T_A(n) (that T_A(n) is O(n (lg n)^{1-kappa})), nor which paper it is or why its machine A is the one meant. 'Replaced by' does not state the result, so the reader cannot tell what bound is being used.
The ratio bound follows by dividing the unstated bound on T_A(n) by n lg n; the reader cannot check it because the bound it depends on is not given on the page.

gaps.term: A is a machine in the fixed-tape model
gaps.quote: So $A$ runs in $o(n\log n)$ time, which contradicts the conjecture that no machine in this model runs in $o(n\log n)$ time.
gaps.note: The contradiction needs A to be a machine in the fixed-tape model that the conjecture quantifies over. The page introduces A as 'the paper's deterministic machine' but never says A has a fixed, finite number of tapes.

gaps.term: Harvey and van der Hoeven bound
gaps.quote: Harvey and van der Hoeven reached $O(n\log n)$, so that order is achievable.
gaps.note: Stated as a fact about the literature without a (cited) marker or a source the reader can check, so the reader cannot verify that O(n log n) is achievable.
